jobs.description:

Join one of the region’s most advanced academic medical centers and help shape critical patient outcomes in a dynamic, mission-driven environment. At SUNY Upstate, your expertise is valued, your voice is heard, and your professional growth is actively supported.

jobs.title: Credit Originations Manager Regional Lead - Community Development Banking - Executive Director
jobs.description:
Job Description

Help scale Affordable and Workforce housing by leading a high-impact origination team within Community Development Banking. You'll shape regional outcomes while partnering with national leaders, client coverage, and credit stakeholders on complex, mission-oriented financings. This role offers executive-level influence, people leadership, and ownership of the client experience across the full origination lifecycle.

As a Credit Originations Manager – Regional Lead, Executive Director within Community Development Banking (CDB), you will lead a regional team responsible for the end-to-end new loan origination process for CDB clients, including evaluating opportunities, structuring transactions, managing the credit approval workflow, and driving disciplined execution through closing and post-close handoff. Your leadership will ensure consistent underwriting quality, strong partnership with Client Executives and Credit/Risk stakeholders, and a high-quality client experience across complex affordable housing construction and permanent lending structures.

In this role, you will be accountable for regional origination outcomes, team leadership, and consistent execution of the CDB credit origination lifecycle (evaluation/structuring, credit approval coordination, documentation/closing leadership, and ongoing transaction-related requests and escalations).

Job Responsibilities

Lead and develop a regional team of Credit Originators, including resource management, performance management, and coverage planning; maintain the ability to directly originate/cover clients when business needs require
Drive results across the region using clear leadership principles (e.g., deliver outcomes, enable the team, lead inclusively, and grow talent)
Evaluate new loan opportunities and guide the team in identifying key strengths/risks to inform decision-making and execution approach
Coach the team on structuring complex affordable/workforce housing loans and coordinating the credit approval process in partnership with Client Executives, Primary Credit Officers, Credit Executives, and Client Associates
Serve as escalation point to unblock the team and drive consistency in term sheet/LOI development, negotiation, documentation execution, and closing readiness (including due diligence coordination and senior management presentations as needed)
Partner with Client Executives to support client strategy execution and ensure originations activity aligns to client objectives and franchise priorities
Provide oversight and challenge on key origination deliverables (e.g., underwriting outputs, credit approval packages/memos, risk rating recommendations), ensuring quality, completeness, and timeliness
Ensure adherence to underwriting standards, approval requirements, and applicable policies/procedures; drive communication and implementation of policy/process updates and best practices across the region
Invest in talent development by training, mentoring, and coaching junior team members and strengthening overall team capabilities

Required Qualifications, Capabilities And Skills

Minimum 10 years of commercial banking/lending experience, including substantial credit structuring, closing, and loan documentation experience
Demonstrated experience structuring and underwriting real estate lending transactions; experience with affordable/workforce housing (preferred focus)
Strong command of credit risk concepts, transaction structuring, and end-to-end execution management
Excellent communication skills; ability to clearly articulate rationale, influence stakeholders, and engage confidently with senior management, clients, and internal partners
Strong interpersonal skills to work effectively with clients, counsel, and cross-functional partners (Credit Risk, legal, closing, construction/disbursement stakeholders)
Significant accounting/finance knowledge and strong analytical and business writing skills
Completion of a major corporate or investment banking credit training program
Proficiency with Microsoft Word, Excel, and PowerPoint
BA/BBA Degree

Preferred Qualifications, Capabilities, And Skills

MBA
Familiarity with JPMorganChase (or similar) policies, procedures, and credit approval systems/processes

ABOUT US

JPMorganChase, one of the oldest financial institutions, offers innovative financial solutions to millions of consumers, small businesses and many of the world's most prominent corporate, institutional and government clients under the J.P. Morgan and Chase brands. Our history spans over 200 years and today we are a leader in investment banking, consumer and small business banking, commercial banking, financial transaction processing and asset management.

We offer a competitive total rewards package including base salary determined based on the role, experience, skill set and location. Those in eligible roles may receive commission-based pay and/or discretionary incentive compensation, paid in the form of cash and/or forfeitable equity, awarded in recognition of individual achievements and contributions. We also offer a range of benefits and programs to meet employee needs, based on eligibility. These benefits include comprehensive health care coverage, on-site health and wellness centers, a retirement savings plan, backup childcare, tuition reimbursement, mental health support, financial coaching and more. Additional details about total compensation and benefits will be provided during the hiring process.

We recognize that our people are our strength and the diverse talents they bring to our global workforce are directly linked to our success. We are an equal opportunity employer and place a high value on diversity and inclusion at our company. We do not discriminate on the basis of any protected attribute, including race, religion, color, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, age, marital or veteran status, pregnancy or disability, or any other basis protected under applicable law. We also make reasonable accommodations for applicants' and employees' religious practices and beliefs, as well as mental health or physical disability needs. Visit our FAQs for more information about requesting an accommodation.

JPMorgan Chase & Co. is an Equal Opportunity Employer, including Disability/Veterans

About The Team

J.P. Morgan's Commercial & Investment Bank is a global leader across banking, markets, securities services and payments. Corporations, governments and institutions throughout the world entrust us with their business in more than 100 countries. The Commercial & Investment Bank provides strategic advice, raises capital, manages risk and extends liquidity in markets around the world.

Oversee operational performance across assigned maternal health access programs.
Maintain a visible presence at partner sites to foster collaborative and consultative client relationships.
Support successful onboarding and implementation of new OBHG programs.
Align hospital and clinic objectives with OBHG services and oversee demonstration of key performance outcomes.

Our mission-driven company offers a unique opportunity to elevate the standard of women's healthcare, providing 24/7 real-time triage and hospital-based obstetric coverage across the United States. We have a strong commitment to equity

The Y actively promotes a culture free from bias and injustice. We are dedicated to removing institutional and systemic barriers that result in oppression and racism. We are looking for a responsible leader who is excited by the prospect of developing and leading the operations of our youth education, childcare or enrichment programs hosted in the Shoreline, Edmonds, and Northshore School Districts. You will be the key player in developing our programs, managing a program budget and working with and leading a team to provide the best programing and services to participants.

Hiring Range:
$80,168.40/Yr.

This is a Regular, Full-Time Role, supporting programs hosted at elementary schools across the Northshore, Edmonds, and Shoreline School Districts.

What you'll get from working at The Y

Membership to the YMCA of Greater Seattle for you and your household
Medical, Dental, Vision, and Life insurance
Retirement with generous employer contributions
Free access to mental health resources
Rapidly-accruing paid time off (PTO) available immediately upon hire

The YMCA of Greater Seattle is committed to providing a positive atmosphere that prioritizes safety and inclusivity for all employees. The YMCA of Greater Seattle has implemented safety standards and protocols related to preventative health measures based on CDC and local health department guidelines.

MMR Vaccination Required
: Licensed School Age Programs require Mumps, Measles and Rubella immunization in accordance with Department of Children, Youth and Family requirements.

Responsibilities

What you'll be doing

Establishes new program activities and expands program(s) within the community in accordance with the Association and branch strategic plans.
Develops and manages the budgets related to the position. Meets fiscal objectives.
Recruits, hires, trains, evaluates and supervises assigned staff and volunteers in assigned areas. Provides development and leadership.

While performing the duties of this job, the employee is regularly required to talk or hear. The employee frequently is required to stand; walk; use hands to finger, handle or feel; and reach with hands and arms. Specific vision abilities required by this job include close vision, distance vision, color vision, peripheral vision, depth perception and ability to adjust focus. This position requires the ability to occasionally lift office products and supplies, up to 20 pounds.

Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

Code of Conduct for Applicants

All employees and volunteers are responsible for adhering to abuse prevention policies, maintaining appropriate boundaries, completing required training, reporting suspicious or inappropriate behavior, and complying with mandated reporting requirements.

Responsible for ensuring staff are properly screened, trained, supervised and held accountable to the organization’s abuse risk management standards.

Qualifications

What we're looking for in an applicant

21 years of age or older.
Bachelor's degree in relevant program area or equivalent education/experience. Other applicable education, training, and experience, which provide the knowledge, abilities, and skills necessary to perform effectively in the position will be considered. Forty-five (45) or more college credits in programming related to child development preferred.
Two years or more years of experience with staff and volunteer supervision, program development, budget management.
Experience and knowledge with youth behavior management and child abuse prevention.
We require pre-employment TB tests and MMR vaccination. To make this process convenient for our new hires, we offer Concentra options at no cost to you.
Intermediate computer skills and experience with Microsoft Office suite.
Ability to visit sites and community organizations.

Preferred Education/Experience

Prefer knowledge of and previous experience with, diverse populations (language, culture, race, physical ability, sexual orientation, etc.). Ability to speak any language in addition to English may be helpful.

You'll be a great fit for the Seattle Y if you:

Thrive on working in a collaborative environment
Are very adaptable
Have high ownership and strong work ethic
Are a great problem solver who can think on your feet
Truly enjoy being of service to people
Like being part of a team that cares about one another as people and enjoy working together
Want to know that the work you do contributes to building a better, stronger community for all

At the Seattle Y, we are an inclusive organization of people with a shared commitment to nurture the potential of youth, promote healthy living, and foster social responsibility. We also believe in supporting the wellbeing of our employees and offer a free Y membership as a benefit of employment.

Become a leader on our team at the YMCA of Greater Seattle where we promote a continuous learning environment and career opportunities.

Director of Advancement Data and Research

Angola, Indiana

Summary

The Director of Advancement Data and Research leads advancement data strategy and operations, serving as the functional owner of Slate CRM, supervising gift processing and donor records, producing reporting and analytics, and directing prospect research and prospect management. This role ensures accurate, secure, and consistent data; delivers actionable donor intelligence and pipeline insights; and supports fundraising effectiveness through strong systems, policies, and staff leadership. This position requires proficiency with AI tools to enhance productivity with duties/projects within the position and department.

Essential Duties And Responsibilities

Slate CRM & Data Governance: Oversight of Slate System for Advancement; establish/enforce data standards, security/access, documentation, and data quality practices; manage imports/updates and data hygiene; train and support users; partner with the Information Technology Office as needed.
Gift Processing & Records: Supervise gift processing to ensure timely, accurate entry of gifts and commitments (gifts, pledges, matching gifts, gifts-in-kind, payroll deductions, adjustments/write-offs/reversals); maintain internal controls and audit-ready documentation; partner with the Business Office as needed.
Reporting & Analytics: Responsible for building and maintaining queries, dashboards, and recurring/ad hoc reports; produce accurate campaign, progress, and financial/analytical reporting; use analytics to inform segmentation, forecasting, and strategy.
Prospect Research: Identify and qualify prospects; produce prospect profiles, wealth/affinity and capacity assessments; manage/validate third-party screening and research resources.
Prospect Management: Oversee prospect assignment and tracking in Slate; optimize portfolios and pipeline health; facilitate portfolio/pipeline review meetings with gift officers.
Collaboration & Support: Provide list pulls for outreach and mailings; support campaign planning; participate in university/advancement events as requested; perform other duties as assigned.
Discretion with confidential information, attention to data integrity, responsibility for protecting sensitive records, donor personal/financial information, and ensuring compliance with data privacy standards.
Continuous Training & Improvement: Actively leverage free Slate Community resources—including groups and learning labs—to strengthen platform expertise. Attend the annual Slate Summit and other role-relevant training courses, as approved by the supervisor.

Education and/or Experience

Bachelor’s degree required; 3-5 years of experience in advancement services/operations, gift processing, prospect research/management, or related roles.

Financial Insurance – employer paid Long Term Disability and voluntary Short-Term Disability, Accident, Hospital Indemnity, and Critical Illness options are available

Retirement – after one year of full-time service you are eligible for an employer contribution of 5% and up to an additional 5% employer match
Education – after 6 months of full-time service, undergraduate education benefits are available for employee, spouse, and dependent children

Salary

The salary is competitive and commensurate with experience and qualifications.

Your leadership will ensure consistent underwriting quality, strong partnership with Client Executives and Credit/Risk stakeholders, and a high-quality client experience across complex affordable housing construction and permanent lending structures.

Invest in talent development by training, mentoring, and coaching junior team members and strengthening overall team capabilities

Required Qualifications, Capabilities And Skills

Minimum 10 years of commercial banking/lending experience, including substantial credit structuring, closing, and loan documentation experience
Demonstrated experience structuring and underwriting real estate lending transactions; experience with affordable/workforce housing (preferred focus)
Strong command of credit risk concepts, transaction structuring, and end-to-end execution management
Excellent communication skills; ability to clearly articulate rationale, influence stakeholders, and engage confidently with senior management, clients, and internal partners

Completion of a major corporate or investment banking credit training program
Proficiency with Microsoft Word, Excel, and PowerPoint

Company Introduction

Free Courses With Certificates is an online education content platform dedicated to providing learners with convenient courses and career development opportunities.

As part of our growth strategy, we are preparing to establish a fintech subsidiary in Chicago. This subsidiary will focus on technology-enabled financial education, enterprise payment solutions, financial management tools, and related support services. Its eventual business activities will depend on the completion of relevant registration, licensing, and regulatory approvals.

Job Overview

We are seeking an experienced Chief Operating Officer (COO) to participate in the planning and establishment of the new subsidiary. The COO will be responsible for developing the operational framework, coordinating with professional advisors and business partners, assembling the initial leadership team, and ensuring the company operates in compliance.

Key Responsibilities
Develop the subsidiary's operational and market access strategy.
Establish internal processes, budgets, controls, and performance standards.
Coordinate and collaborate with legal, compliance, accounting, and technology advisors.
Support necessary registration, licensing reviews, and regulatory preparations.
Recruit and manage the initial operations team.
Evaluate vendors, technology systems, and strategic partnerships.
Implement risk management, data protection, and compliance procedures.

Report progress, risks, and operational results to senior leadership.

Qualifications
Bachelor's degree in business, finance, accounting, law, or a related field; advanced degrees preferred.

At least 10 years of executive or senior operations management experience.

Experience in financial services, fintech, payments, compliance, or new business startup.

Familiarity with U.S. financial regulations and operational risk control.

Strong leadership, budgeting, negotiation, and project management skills.

Able to work in Chicago or travel regularly.

Compensation and Benefits

Competitive executive compensation based on experience.

Performance-based bonuses.

Medical, dental, and vision insurance.

401(k) retirement plan.

Paid leave and company vacation.

Flexible mixed work arrangements.

Professional development support.

Opportunity to help build a new subsidiary from its early stages.

Director of Advancement Data and Research

Careers

A Great Place to Work!

Director of Advancement Data and Research

Angola, Indiana

Summary

The Director of Advancement Data and Research leads advancement data strategy and operations, serving as the functional owner of Slate CRM, supervising gift processing and donor records, producing reporting and analytics, and directing prospect research and prospect management. This role ensures accurate, secure, and consistent data; delivers actionable donor intelligence and pipeline insights; and supports fundraising effectiveness through strong systems, policies, and staff leadership. This position requires proficiency with AI tools to enhance productivity with duties/projects within the position and department.

Essential Duties And Responsibilities

Slate CRM & Data Governance: Oversight of Slate System for Advancement; establish/enforce data standards, security/access, documentation, and data quality practices; manage imports/updates and data hygiene; train and support users; partner with the Information Technology Office as needed.
Gift Processing & Records: Supervise gift processing to ensure timely, accurate entry of gifts and commitments (gifts, pledges, matching gifts, gifts-in-kind, payroll deductions, adjustments/write-offs/reversals); maintain internal controls and audit-ready documentation; partner with the Business Office as needed.
Reporting & Analytics: Responsible for building and maintaining queries, dashboards, and recurring/ad hoc reports; produce accurate campaign, progress, and financial/analytical reporting; use analytics to inform segmentation, forecasting, and strategy.
Prospect Research: Identify and qualify prospects; produce prospect profiles, wealth/affinity and capacity assessments; manage/validate third-party screening and research resources.
Prospect Management: Oversee prospect assignment and tracking in Slate; optimize portfolios and pipeline health; facilitate portfolio/pipeline review meetings with gift officers.
Collaboration & Support: Provide list pulls for outreach and mailings; support campaign planning; participate in university/advancement events as requested; perform other duties as assigned.
Discretion with confidential information, attention to data integrity, responsibility for protecting sensitive records, donor personal/financial information, and ensuring compliance with data privacy standards.
Continuous Training & Improvement: Actively leverage free Slate Community resources—including groups and learning labs—to strengthen platform expertise. Attend the annual Slate Summit and other role-relevant training courses, as approved by the supervisor.

Education and/or Experience

Bachelor’s degree required; 3-5 years of experience in advancement services/operations, gift processing, prospect research/management, or related roles.

Outstanding Benefits

Benefits

Trine University offers a comprehensive benefit package designed to provide a variety of choices to best fit your needs and the needs of your family. Some benefits offered include:

Health – medical, dental, vision, flex spending, HSA accounts
Life Insurance – a variety of voluntary life options are available along with an employer paid employee life policy valued at 1½ times annual salary
Financial Insurance – employer paid Long Term Disability and voluntary Short-Term Disability, Accident, Hospital Indemnity, and Critical Illness options are available
Paid vacation and sick time
Retirement – after one year of full-time service you are eligible for an employer contribution of 5% and up to an additional 5% employer match
Education – after 6 months of full-time service, undergraduate education benefits are available for employee, spouse, and dependent children

Salary

The salary is competitive and commensurate with experience and qualifications.
